findings.issue: The word きごう ('symbol') was inserted three times into the phonetic transcription — the tokenizer emitted きごう as the 'reading' of the space characters. きごう is not pronounced; the kana string has extra syllables.
findings.current: わたしわきごううたをきごううたうのがきごうへたです
findings.suggested: わたしわうたをうたうのがへたです

findings.issue: Same space-token bug leaked into romaji: 'kigou' inserted three times. This is not the known punctuation/katakana issue — it adds pronounced syllables that do not exist in the sentence.

も means 'also/too' (rain is one more problem added to the cold), not 'still'. 'It's still raining' implies it was already raining, which the JP does not say. The expl_en itself correctly glosses も as 'too'.
findings.current: It's cold today. On top of that, it's still raining.
findings.suggested: It's cold today. On top of that, it's raining too.

findings.issue: Mesmo problema da versão en: も = 'também', não 'ainda'. 'Ainda está chovendo' lê-se como 'still raining' (a chuva já vinha antes), sentido que o JP não tem. A própria expl_pt glosa も como 'também'.
findings.current: Hoje está frio. Além disso, ainda está chovendo.
findings.suggested: Hoje está frio. Além disso, também está chovendo.

findings.issue: Space token (s: " ") carries reading きごう ('symbol' — tokenizer class label, not a reading). A space has no reading. Same defect at tokens[5].r and tokens[9].r. This is the source of the kana/romaji corruption.

この means only 'this' (near speaker); 'that' belongs to その/あの. The English gloss 'this, that' teaches a wrong demonstrative range. (The pt 'este, esse' is fine given Brazilian colloquial usage.)

明るい = 'bright/light', not 'clear' (cloudless). The record's own token gloss and expl_en say 'bright/luminous'; the main translation contradicts them. (pt 'claro' is fine since it covers 'bright' in Portuguese.)
findings.current: The sky to the south is clear.
findings.suggested: The sky to the south is bright.

findings.issue: The explanation says 'Compare with the next sentence, which uses the intransitive 消える' — but sentences live standalone in the bank and are referenced by ID; there is no guaranteed 'next sentence'. Dangling cross-reference confuses learners.
findings.current: Compare with the next sentence, which uses the intransitive 消える.
findings.suggested: Compare with the intransitive 消える ('to go out by itself').

findings.issue: Same dangling reference as expl_en: 'Compare com a frase seguinte' assumes an ordering that the standalone sentence bank does not guarantee.
findings.current: Compare com a frase seguinte, que usa o intransitivo 消える.
findings.suggested: Compare com o intransitivo 消える ('apagar-se sozinho').
